data.name: Selim
data.gender_notes: Selim is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Turkish word "selâm", meaning peace or security, and the Arabic word "lim", meaning moon. In Islamic tradition, Selim is the name of two sultans known for their military victories and peace treaties. In Christianity, Selim is believed to be the name of a saint who lived during the Byzantine era. The name Selim carries the meaning “Moon” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Selim usually hope their child will grow to embody moon and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the peaceful and calming presence of the moon and the security it provides.
data.etymology: Selim belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Moon.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Selim total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

in_hebrew.name: שְׁלִים
in_hebrew.long_meaning: שְׁלִים הוא שם עברי שמשמעותו אהבה ושלום, שלמות, שלוש. השם נמצא במקרא, כאשר בתהילים, פרק 85, פסוק 11, האלוהים מכונים 'שומר-שלים' (שומר השלום). בנוסף, השם 'שלים' הוא גם שם של נביא יהודי, שהוזכר בספר נחום, פרק 1, פסוק 4. השם 'שלים' נחשב לשם נוצרי, אך גם בקהילה היהודית, השם 'שלים' נחשב לשם נבון, משום שהוא מכיל את המונח 'שלום' אשר הוא חלק מברכת 'שלום-עליכם'.

in_greek.name: Σηλὴμ
in_greek.long_meaning: Ο Σηλὴμ είναι ονομασία με ελληνική ρίζα. Η λέξη έχει την έννοια της ελπίδας, της ειρήνης και του τέλους. Ο Σηλὴμ είναι επίσης ένα ονομαστικό με ελληνική ρίζα, που εμφανίζεται στην Καινή Διαθήκη, στο βιβλίο του Ματθαίου, στη φρασική 'η ελπίς του Παναγίου' (Μαθ. 1:21) και στη φρασική 'Σηλὴμ τὸ όνομα του' (Μαθ. 1:25).

in_latin.name: Selim
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Selim significat spem, pacem, et finem. Inscriptio nominis Selim in Novo Testamento, in libro Matthaei, versu 1:21, ubi dicitur 'Spes Dei' (Spes Dei). Et in versu 1:25, ubi dicitur 'Selim nomen ejus' (Selim nomen ejus).

in_english.name: Selim
in_english.long_meaning: The name Selim is a shortened form of the Hebrew name Shelim, meaning hope, peace, and completeness. The name is derived from the Hebrew word 'shalem', which means 'whole' or 'complete'. In biblical times, the name Selim was associated with the prophets, and it is also mentioned in the book of Isaiah (Isaiah 1:4). The name Selim is also associated with the saint name of Saint Selim, an early Christian saint. In modern times, the name Selim is used in various Christian cultures, and it is often associated with qualities such as hope, peace, and completeness.

data.cultural_impact: The name Selim is of Middle Eastern origin and holds significant cultural importance in Turkey and the Islamic world. The name is reminiscent of the history of two great sultans - Selim I (1512-1520), who expanded the Ottoman Empire, and Selim II (1566-1574), who cemented its position as a major European power. Selim is also the name of the sixth caliph of the Sunni Islamic tradition, Selim II (1566-1574), and the name of the last Ottoman Sultan, Selim III (1757-1808), who tried to reform the Ottoman Empire.
data.spiritual_significance: In Christianity, Selim is believed to be the name of a saint whose significant deeds and life remain mostly unknown. However, his name holds spiritual importance for those who bear it as it is associated with the divine qualities of peace and security. The name Selim can serve as a reminder to its bearers of the lasting peace and security that comes from a deep and abiding faith in God. It is a name that can inspire its bearer to strive for peace in their personal lives and in the world around them. Ultimately, the name Selim can be seen as a reflection of the Christian belief that God is the source of all peace and security, and that ultimately, only in God can we find true and lasting peace.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Selim in Christian tradition symbolizes peace and deliverance. This name is derived from the Hebrew term "shalom," meaning completeness or wholeness, and was borne by several saints who lived in times of war and turmoil, offering peace and salvation to their communities.

biblical_reference.note: The name Selim is associated with the concept of hope and peace in the Hebrew Bible.

historical_references.reference: Sultan Selim I, also known as Selim the Grim or Selim the Forceful, ruled the Ottoman Empire from 1512 to 1520. He undertook several successful military campaigns, expanding the Ottoman territories through the Balkans and the Middle East. Selim played a significant role in the decline of the Byzantine Empire and the rise of the Ottoman Empire as a major power in Europe and the Mediterranean.

Sultan Selim II, also known as Selim the Sot or Selim the Drunkard, ruled the Ottoman Empire from 1566 to 1574. He is known for his construction of the New Mosque in Istanbul and his patronage of the arts. Selim's military campaigns were less successful than those of his predecessors, leading to the loss of some Ottoman territories in the Caucasus and the Balkans.
